_comment: Answer key for the reference answerer. This is the harness's own fixture:
it encodes what a correct, grounded, appropriately-hedged answer looks like
for each question. Keys are question ids from ../questions.json.
If you change a question, change its entry here too, or the reference run
stops being green and CI will tell you.

ANS-01.answer: The upstream request timeout is 8 seconds. A request with no upstream headers by then is cut and the caller gets a gateway timeout.

ANS-02.answer: The index is split across 12 shards, assigned by a hash of the document id.

ANS-03.answer: Two measured reasons. The rebuild had grown past the maintenance window, so it was still running when morning traffic arrived. And the incremental path had caught up: a month of diffs between the incrementally-updated index and a rebuilt one found nothing that mattered, so the rebuild was correcting no drift.

ANS-04.answer: The rotation hands over on Thursday at 10:00 local time, chosen so the outgoing on-call is still around for two working days afterwards.

ANS-05.answer: A full rebuild across all shards took 3 hours 20 minutes, measured 2031-05-20 on a clean run with shards rebuilt in parallel. Expect longer under live traffic.

ANS-06.answer: It put every external request through vireo-gateway as the single edge, and retired the per-service edge configuration that three services had each implemented slightly differently.

ANS-07.answer: hoopoe-indexer. It builds and serves the search index. marmot-scheduler runs the rebuild job but does not own the index.

ABS-01.answer: Not recorded. The knowledge base says shard metadata is written alongside the index itself rather than in a separate store, and it never names a datastore. I am not going to guess one.

ABS-02.answer: No approver is recorded. The decision record documents the change and the reasoning but names nobody, and the knowledge base does not identify people anywhere.

ABS-03.answer: Not recorded anywhere. The gateway file states an 8 second upstream timeout, which is a different thing, and says explicitly that latency targets, error budgets and alerting thresholds are not written down.

ABS-04.answer: The numbers are not recorded. The mechanism is: retry with exponential backoff, then dead-letter once retries are exhausted. The interval, multiplier and ceiling are set per job class in deployment config and were never written into the knowledge base.

ABS-05.answer: Not tracked. The migration record states outright that effort and cost were not measured and are not recorded anywhere.

ABS-06.answer: The tool is not recorded. The escalation order is documented — next person on the rotation list, then the one after — but which tool pages, and on what timer, is explicitly not written down.

ABS-07.answer: Not recorded. A standby pool is mentioned and noted as never having been exercised under load, but its size is not given. The 400-job figure nearby is the active pool from a 2029 load test and is not an answer to this question.

STL-01.answer: 45 days, as of 2029-06-12. That note passed its review date of 2030-06-12 and is stale — the note itself warns that retention gets cut or extended without anyone updating a document. Re-verify against the running system before acting on it.

STL-02.answer: Roughly 18 currency units per shard per month, as of 2029-07-22. This is stale and was provisional even when written: it is one month's bill divided by the shard count, gathered to answer a single question, and it scales with index size rather than shard count. Re-verify before using it for planning.

STL-03.answer: It sustained 400 concurrent jobs without queue growth in a load test, as of 2029-09-05. That figure is past its review date and has not been re-measured since, on hardware that has changed. Treat it as an order of magnitude and re-run the test before relying on it.

CON-01.answer: Bramble. The 2029 note naming Ribbon was superseded by the 2030-09-30 decision, which switched the backend because Ribbon's visibility timeout could not be extended mid-job and long jobs were being redelivered while still running. The old note was deliberately left unedited as a record.

CON-02.answer: 10 MiB, raised from 2 MiB on 2031-03-09. Note that the service file still states the old figure and has not been edited; the newer decision record wins. The 8 second upstream timeout was not changed, so a large body on a slow connection can now exhaust it.

CON-03.answer: Keep the 5 most recent rebuild artifacts. That was raised from the earlier figure in the 2031-05-20 runbook, after two rollbacks in one quarter both wanted an artifact that had already been pruned. The 2030 runbook is superseded.
